text:
I couldn't get usable details from the review pages. RTINGS, Tom's Guide and What Hi-Fi? loaded without their article text, and Good Housekeeping and Best Products blocked the fetch. So the picks below come from my general knowledge, not from those reviews. Check specs and prices before you buy.

**Models worth considering**
- **JBL Flip 7** is a safe all-round pick. It's a mid-size speaker that should be IP68-rated (dustproof and waterproof). It has good bass for its size and is easy to carry. RTINGS lists it as a popular model, though I couldn't confirm that page's verdict. [Search JBL Flip 7 on Amazon](https://www.amazon.com/s?k=JBL+Flip+7)
- **Bose SoundLink Flex (2nd Gen)** has a clear, balanced sound and a rugged build. It's also on RTINGS's popular list. [Search Bose SoundLink Flex 2nd Gen on Amazon](https://www.amazon.com/s?k=Bose+SoundLink+Flex+2nd+Gen)
- **soundcore Boom 2 Plus** is a bigger, louder speaker for a group at the beach. A deal page lists it at $249.99, or about $200 with code AFSC20 at Soundcore's US store. That page is a coupon-tracking site, and I haven't confirmed the code still works. [Dealectric listing](https://dealectric.com/go/soundcore-boom-2-plus)

**What to look for**
- **Rating:** IP67 or IP68 covers splashes and dunks.
- **Floating:** a speaker that floats is handy at the pool, so check for this.
- **Size:** compact speakers are easy to carry. Larger ones are louder outdoors.
- **Battery:** aim for 12 hours or more for a full day.

If you tell me your budget and whether you need it to float, I can narrow this to one pick.
